title: Economics defaults and consumption guardrails — developer-facing brief
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This brief describes the recommended out-of-the-box economics defaults and consumption guardrails we will surface in the Redwood Console, SDKs, and self-serve API during developer onboarding. The goal is to make the first 30 days of usage predictable for teams integrating Redwood while preserving easy paths to increase fidelity or migrate to Dedicated/Private. This is a developer-facing, operationally-actionable doc intended for Product, Growth, and Developer Experience teams.

Why this matters

- New integrations frequently cause surprise billing or unexpected latency spikes.
- Defaulting to safe, opinionated consumption settings reduces churn and support load.
- Defaults should balance unit-cost efficiency while exposing clear upgrade paths (warm capacity, reserved bundles, fidelity addons).

Scope

- Surface defaults in: Console onboarding, SDK quickstarts, REST API serverless defaults, and the hosted API free tier.
- Cover: request throttling, streaming length caps, batch/sequence defaults, KV/prefix cache TTLs, embeddings retention, fallback model selection for capacity shortfalls, and grace policies for failed requests.

Design principles

1. Predictability: If a developer does nothing, their bill and latency profile should be predictable for small-to-medium workloads.
2. Safety: Prevent runaway cost patterns (infinite loops, exponential backoffs).
3. Discoverability: Provide simple UI hints and an in-console cost estimator before first production call.
4. Escalation path: Make it easy to request higher throughput (self-serve + quick sales assist).

Default configuration (recommended baseline)

| Area | Default | Rationale | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Free Tier monthly allowance | 100k token generation + 10k embedding units | Enough to evaluate features and run small demos | Visible on Console billing panel |
| Max streaming response length | 1024 tokens | Prevents long-tail runaway costs | SDKs show warning at 800 tokens |
| Default max tokens per request (non-stream) | 512 tokens | Reasonable tradeoff of latency and cost for quick APIs | Per-route overrides allowed |
| Default batching window (hosted) | 8 ms / 64 requests (whichever triggers first) | Low-latency baseline that enables batching benefits | Tunable by tenancy and route |
| KV/prefix cache TTL (session cache) | 15 minutes | Reduces repeated prefix cost without stale responses | Eviction metrics emitted |
| Embeddings retention (hosted) | 30 days, auto-tier to cold storage | Limits storage costs for exploratory users | Upgradeable via contract |
| Soft cost threshold alert | 60% of monthly free+subscription estimate | Early signal to user and console tips | Triggers in-app education modal |
| Hard cost throttle (per-route) | 200% of budgeted rate or absolute 1M tokens/day | Prevents runaway with explicit user consent to override | Admin-only override in Console |
| Default fallback mapping | Balance: smaller, cheaper variant within same architecture family | Keeps requests alive at lower fidelity under contention | See fallback table below |

Fallback model mapping (example)

- family: redwood-xl -> fallback: redwood-large-quantized (latency + cost benefit)
- family: open-llama-70b -> fallback: open-llama-13b-quant (compatible with streaming?)

Operational rollout plan

1. Phase 0 — Internal Canary (2 weeks): Console + SDK telemetry only, internal accounts. Verify billing events and alerting.
2. Phase 1 — Beta customers (6 weeks): opt-in on Console; collect churn, support touchpoints.
3. Phase 2 — Auto-enroll on new sign-ups (4 weeks): default applied to all new tenants; monitor top-20 tenants for regressions.
4. Phase 3 — Global rollout: enable for all; provide migration playbook for existing customers.

Ownership and SLAs

- Default policy implementation: product (Maya Chen) + eng-platform (owner: Arjun Patel).
- Billing visibility and alerts: finance-legal (owner: Claire Huang).
- SLOs to monitor:
  - p50 latency for interactive endpoints <= 120 ms (goal)
  - p95 latency <= 450 ms for default routes
  - error rate <= 0.5% attributable to defaults (goal)
  - percent of tenants who hit soft threshold < 6% in first 30 days (target)

Migration guidance for existing customers

1. Identify customers who have custom route configs or disabled defaults.
2. Share a migration checklist with per-customer recommendations (see Related: onboarding-and-cost-advisor-playbook).
3. Support path: self-serve migration toggles in Console + white-glove conversions for enterprise customers.

Developer-facing UX patterns

- Console preflight: before first production request, show a cost estimate card with the defaults and toggle to preview higher throughput.
- SDK warnings: log a single warning when request size/stream length exceeds 75% of default. Include quick-link to Console.
- API response hint: if request is throttled or fallen back to cheaper variant, include a structured header: X-Redwood-Fallback: <variant-id>, X-Redwood-Cost-Estimate: <tokens,approx-cents>.

QA & Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests for default config present and loaded in Console/SDK (coverage >= 90% for config-loading paths).
- Integration test that simulates 10k requests with a 95th percentile latency within p95 targets.
- Billing simulator run using synthetic workloads to verify alerts at 60% and hard throttle at configured thresholds.

Example SDK / YAML snippet (developer quickstart)

```yaml
# Included in SDK quickstart and Console sample config
redwood:
  defaults:
    max_tokens: 512
    streaming_max: 1024
    batching:
      window_ms: 8
      max_requests: 64
    cache:
      session_ttl_minutes: 15
    alerts:
      soft_pct: 60
      hard_pct: 200
```

API example with fallback hint (HTTP response header example)

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Fallback: redwood-large-quantized
X-Redwood-Estimated-Tokens: 430

Customer communication templates

- Pre-enrollment email: short explanation of defaults, link to cost estimator, how to opt-out.
- In-product modal: one-click preview of how consuming 10k tokens would impact monthly estimate.
- For enterprise: tailored migration proposal with expected delta on commitments and SKU recommendations.

Open questions / risks

1. Quantization compatibility: need sign-off from runtime team on which quantized variants are safe for streaming.
2. Edge cases: conversational apps that keep long-running sessions may hit cache TTLs frequently — recommend session pinning option for dedicated customers.
3. Support load: initial rollout may increase tickets around false positives from soft alerts.

Next steps / action items

- Product to finalize default numbers in collaboration with Finance and Runtime by 2026-06-01 (Owner: Maya Chen).
- Eng-platform to expose config flags and telemetry hooks by 2026-06-22 (Owner: Arjun Patel).
- Console team to implement preflight estimator and modal by 2026-07-05 (Owner: Sofia Ramirez).
- Growth to prepare customer messaging and FAQ by 2026-07-12 (Owner: Ellie Thompson).

Appendix — telemetry events to emit

- defaults.applied (tenant_id, defaults_version)
- cost_alert.soft_triggered (tenant_id, pct_of_estimate)
- cost_throttle.hard_applied (tenant_id, route_id, reason)
- fallback.used (tenant_id, original_variant, fallback_variant, tokens_saved)

References

- See pricing-and-packaging/predictive-bundling-algorithm (internal) for bundling heuristics.
- See product-overview/onboarding-and-cost-advisor-playbook for customer migration templates.
- See design-specs/quantization-rollout-observability for quantization compatibility checklist.

If you have questions or want to propose different baseline values, file a comment below or ping the owners listed above.
